hypothesis: Disable CTS sink clustering (size/diameter = 0) so the clock tree is built without clustering-induced detours and extra buffers; this reduces clock insertion delay/skew and clock-buffer congestion, leaving more routing resources and slack headroom for the propagated-clock setup paths that determine full-flow WNS/TNS, while keeping overflow well under 300.
analysis: Hypothesis not supported: disabling CTS sink clustering worsened WNS in all three cases (dWNS −15.8%, −8.9%, −3.1%), with only TNS improving slightly (+4.5%, +5.6%, +10.1%) and overflow staying low (~99–122). The WNS degradation suggests removing clustering increased clock insertion delay/skew or buffer count rather than reducing detours, hurting propagated-clock setup paths. Next step: sweep small nonzero size/diameter values (e.g., 5–20 µm) to retain clustering benefits while trimming detours, and re-evaluate WNS/TNS.
